questions.prompt: Roughly what fraction of US equity trading volume is executed by algorithms?
questions.explanation: About three-quarters — up from roughly 25% in 2005.

questions.prompt: In Colab, what must you do first so your edits to a course notebook are saved?
options: File → Save a copy in Drive
questions.explanation: Course notebooks are read-only templates. 'Save a copy in Drive' makes it yours.

questions.prompt: Which of these belongs on the AI Red List?
options: Providing a statistic without a source
questions.explanation: LLMs invent numbers confidently. Every figure needs a source you can click.

questions.prompt: What is a 'tracer bullet' in this course's vocabulary?
options: A fast way to write loops
Testing code on a case whose answer you already know
questions.explanation: Verify on a hand-checkable input before trusting code on real data.

questions.prompt: What is the local install command for Jupyter in this course?
questions.explanation: We deliberately avoid Anaconda — two pip commands do the job.

questions.prompt: Why do solution notebooks unlock only after you submit an attempt?
options: Because attempt-first learning is what makes skills stick
To prevent cheating on the certificate
questions.explanation: Reading a solution feels like learning; producing one is learning.

questions.prompt: Why does every exercise ask for an AI-usage disclosure?
options: To build the professional habit — undisclosed AI in a financial model is a compliance incident
questions.explanation: Disclosure is normal professional practice in regulated finance.
